punchline: Before he was a Navy SEAL, David Goggins spent childhood nights working at his violent father's roller rink.
thirty_sec: David Goggins grew up with a violent father and worked late nights at the family roller rink as a little boy. After his mom fled with him to small-town Indiana, he faced racism and poverty, and he copied his way through school. His book doesn't pretend any of that was minor. It asks you to write your own bad cards down, because living as their victim was what kept him stuck. He went on to become a Navy SEAL.
question: What's one hard thing from your past that ended up giving you something useful?
